subject: Can evaluating a promise invalidate a ptr to a binding?

messages.author: c0f3a574a1033b64
messages.subject: Can evaluating a promise invalidate a ptr to a binding?
parts:
In Environment.h, there is the comment:
   // Invoke read monitor (if any) only if
   // forcedValue() did not force a Promise.  (If a
   // Promise was forced, the read monitor will have
   // been invoked anyway, and 'bdg' may now be
   // junk.)

What's the concern here?  IIUC, adding and removing symbols from the environment doesn't invalidate pointers to bindings, and it seems reasonable to assume that the environment isn't going to be garbage collected here.  The only thing I can think of is users doing nasty things like:
       delayedAssign("x", { rm("x") })

Am I missing something here?

Thanks
